requirements.requirement: opsadmin user exists on node1 with the specified ed25519 public key installed for SSH access
requirements.summary: Baseline confirmed opsadmin did not exist (cmd-f784a01603fe48d0). Executor created opsadmin, wrote the exact provided key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys with 700/600 permissions and correct ownership, and verified via id/cat (cmd-b8f4affd15ec4e8f). The account, key, and permissions were reconfirmed identically after a full node restart (cmd-24db8af671f84d47, cmd-42ee30ca97e54988), showing the configuration is persistent, not just transiently applied.

requirements.requirement: SSH authentication on node1 requires key-based auth (password/challenge-response auth disabled, pubkey auth enabled) sshd-wide
requirements.summary: Baseline already showed PasswordAuthentication no / PubkeyAuthentication yes / ChallengeResponseAuthentication no in sshd_config (cmd-f784a01603fe48d0); executor explicitly reaffirmed these directives, validated with sshd -t, and restarted the ssh service (cmd-b8f4affd15ec4e8f). Additionally opsadmin's local password was locked with passwd -l, removing any password-based fallback for that account specifically. Settings were verified unchanged both immediately after configuration and after a full node reboot (cmd-24db8af671f84d47, cmd-42ee30ca97e54988).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1: healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id e4e401d2..., active sshd, opsadmin/key state, and listening port 22 (cmd-24db8af671f84d47). Reboot was issued with an ack returned before disconnect (cmd-cdbcf0b9c7324f19), a connection-refused window was observed during the restart (cmd-2a724120b19e44c8), and a new boot_id ee3dd910... was confirmed post-restart (cmd-884ec694cd7249be). Post-restart recovery of sshd, auth directives, opsadmin account/key/password-lock, and port 22 listener was verified (cmd-42ee30ca97e54988). This matches the fixed after_executor snapshot's independent boot-identity observation, which cross-checks against the executor's own reported values.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes — creating opsadmin with the specified key and enforcing key-based-only SSH auth — are directly satisfied and persisted across a verified full node restart. The mandatory restart evidence protocol was also completed with a coherent pre/post boot-identity transition that cross-checks against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary mutations or hygiene issues were identified.
limitations: PasswordAuthentication/PubkeyAuthentication were already set correctly in the baseline sshd_config before the executor acted, so the executor's contribution here was reaffirmation and verification rather than an initial change; this does not affect satisfaction of the final required state.

No live SSH login attempt (with the private key or a password) was captured to directly prove end-to-end authentication behavior; conclusions rely on sshd_config directives, sshd -t validation, and file/permission state rather than an actual authentication test.

operational_hygiene.summary: All seven executor commands map clearly to task purposes: discovery/baseline (cmd-f784a01603fe48d0), account+key+sshd configuration (cmd-b8f4affd15ec4e8f), pre-restart baseline capture (cmd-24db8af671f84d47), restart issuance (cmd-cdbcf0b9c7324f19), restart-window/recovery polling (cmd-2a724120b19e44c8, cmd-884ec694cd7249be), and post-restart verification (cmd-42ee30ca97e54988). No unnecessary, unbounded, or unreverted mutations were found. The one nonzero exit (cmd-2a724120b19e44c8, connection refused) is expected discovery during the reboot window, not a failure. The only state changes shown in the lifecycle diff (boot identity and systemd-private tmp dirs) are natural consequences of the reboot itself, not executor residue.
